introduction: Identify the repeated outer-to-inner relationship before using a close-up feature to support the organ interpretation. This H&E image and the thymus detail are different specimens, not a matched magnification sequence.

data.title: Thymus architecture: relate cortex, medulla and partitions

regions.label: Darker peripheral tissue
regions.observation: The marked dark band lies outside a paler inner field. Similar dark-to-pale relationships recur elsewhere in the photograph.
regions.interpretation: In this provider-identified thymus, the peripheral, densely nuclear tissue supports cortical organisation. Compare its location with the paler inner region rather than naming a dark patch in isolation.
regions.limit: This H&E field cannot identify the selection state or immunophenotype of an individual thymocyte.

regions.label: Paler inner tissue
regions.observation: The marked inner field is paler than the nearby peripheral band and lies within the same local lobular pattern.
regions.interpretation: Its position and contrast support a medullary region. Relate the inner and outer compartments before turning to the separate detail photograph for an epithelial whorl.
regions.limit: A pale centre alone is not a germinal centre, nor does this one two-dimensional field establish the full three-dimensional continuity of the medulla.

regions.label: Pink connective partition
regions.observation: A branching pink band separates nearby lymphoid-rich areas. Follow its course rather than treating it as the outer boundary of the entire organ.
regions.interpretation: This relationship supports an internal connective partition in the lobular thymic pattern. It helps orient cortex and medulla across the wider field.
regions.limit: The complete capsule is outside this view. Not every pink or round profile is a partition or a Hassall corpuscle; vessel walls and lumina need separate assessment.

data.model: Repeated darker peripheral tissue surrounds paler inner fields, with connective partitions between neighbouring areas. Together with the provider’s thymus identification, those spatial relationships support a cortical–medullary, lobular interpretation. Use the separate detail photograph to inspect epithelial whorls, while keeping the specimens and preparation records distinct. This field supplies more architecture than a close-up but does not show the complete organ boundary or establish cell lineage.

introduction: A concentric epithelial whorl and a lymphoid follicle are different structures. This is a detail field, not a whole-organ survey.

data.title: Thymus detail: inspect a whorl before naming a compartment

regions.label: Concentric epithelial whorl
regions.observation: A rounded pale profile in the upper-left field contains visible concentric layering.
regions.interpretation: In the supplied thymic context, this layered epithelial appearance supports a Hassall corpuscle. Compare the organisation of the profile, not simply its colour, with a lymphoid follicle.
regions.limit: Not every round or brown profile in this image is a corpuscle; other profiles require their own boundary and content assessment.

regions.label: Paler tissue near the whorls
regions.observation: Several pale, layered profiles occupy a field less densely packed with small dark nuclei than nearby tissue.
regions.interpretation: The combination of epithelial whorls and their neighbourhood supports a medullary-type field in this creator-identified thymus.
regions.limit: The crop does not map a complete lobule or prove that every paler area belongs to one continuous medulla.

regions.label: Lymphocyte-rich field
regions.observation: Many small, dark nuclear profiles form a densely crowded area in the lower-right field.
regions.interpretation: Compare the density with the whorl-containing field. Use surrounding organisation to build the thymic argument rather than treating one dark patch as an entire organ.
regions.limit: Nuclear darkness cannot establish the developmental or selection stage of each thymocyte.

data.model: Concentric epithelial whorls occur in a relatively pale field alongside crowded small-nuclear tissue. In the supplied thymic specimen, that arrangement supports a Hassall-corpuscle and medullary-type interpretation. A whole-section view would be needed to establish the complete lobular pattern. Adult appearance does not reveal each cell’s developmental lineage or selection history.

introduction: Identify a relationship: vessel, surrounding lymphoid tissue, and neighbouring tissue. This is a detail field, not a whole-organ survey.

data.title: Spleen detail: follow a vessel and its neighbourhood

regions.label: Vascular profile and surrounding cells
regions.observation: A small lumen with an enclosing wall lies within a densely cellular field.
regions.interpretation: In the creator-identified spleen, inspect how the vessel relates to the adjacent lymphoid-rich tissue. A vessel-associated lymphoid compartment supports the white-pulp interpretation.
regions.limit: This detail does not trace the vessel through serial sections, establish every branch, or identify surrounding T and B cells individually.

regions.label: Dense lymphoid-rich field
regions.observation: Closely packed small, dark nuclear profiles occupy much of the lower-right field.
regions.interpretation: Compare their density and arrangement with the less densely lymphoid tissue to the left. This supports a compartment comparison within the supplied splenic context.
regions.limit: Darkness alone does not identify a germinal centre, a specific lymphocyte subtype or an activation state.

regions.label: Less densely lymphoid field
regions.observation: The left-hand field has a more mixed cellular appearance than the densely packed region to the right.
regions.interpretation: Use this contrast together with a wider splenic view when relating the regions to red and white pulp. Describe the visible tissue before naming an individual channel.
regions.limit: The image does not securely resolve every sinusoid wall. A pale interval is not, by itself, proof of a vascular sinusoid.

data.model: The field contains a small vascular profile within densely cellular tissue, beside a less densely lymphoid region. These spatial relationships fit the supplied splenic provenance and support a white-pulp/red-pulp comparison. A wider field is still needed to map the overall distribution; the detail does not identify every lymphocyte subtype or every sinusoid boundary.
